title: Relationships
about: Collocations about friendship and love: making and keeping friends, kinds of friends, and the language of a love story, such as strike up a friendship, keep in touch, mutual friends, love at first sight and accept a proposal.

parts.title: More with love, friend and relationship
parts.note: Завдання з книжки: знайти у словнику ще по два сполучення до love, friend, friendship і relationship. Ось ті, що трапляються найчастіше. Зверни увагу на дієслова: дружбу цінують — value, руку дружби простягають — hold out, стосунки завершують — end. А «передавай привіт» близькій людині англійською часто звучить як send sb your love: Send your mum my love.

rows: He loved his wife deeply and still talks about her every day.
Grandma sends her love and says thank you for the flowers.
My best friend and I have had coffee together every Friday for ten years.
It was lovely to see an old friend at my cousin's wedding.
She married a childhood friend from her village.
A true friend helps you move house without complaining.
That summer camp was the start of a lasting friendship.
hold out the hand of friendship
After years of arguing about the fence, our neighbour held out the hand of friendship.
I really value your friendship, so I want to be honest with you.
He ended the relationship by text, which upset her even more.
Long working hours can put a strain on family relationships.

items.pattern: make friends (with sb) · make new friends · make a friend
items.meaning: start a friendship with someone; get to know people who become your friends
items.example: Our daughter was nervous about her new school, but she **made friends** on the very first day.
more: My grandad **made friends with** half the village after he joined the bowls club.
It can be hard to **make new friends** when you move to another city as an adult.
items.watchOut: «Знайти друзів» англійською зазвичай make friends, а не find friends чи get friends (це типові помилки учнів). «Подружитися з кимось» — make friends with sb, і friends тут у множині, навіть якщо друг один: I made friends with Olha.

items.pattern: strike up a friendship (with sb) · strike – struck – struck · also strike up a conversation
items.meaning: start a friendship, often by chance, with someone you have just met
items.example: At the hairdresser's, my mum **struck up a friendship** with the woman in the next chair, and they still phone each other every week.
more: The two dog owners **struck up a friendship** in the park, and now they walk together every morning.
My dad will **strike up a conversation** with anyone, from the postman to the dentist.
items.watchOut: Strike тут не про удар і не про страйк: strike up — зав'язати знайомство чи розмову, часто випадково, з людиною, яку щойно зустрів. Форми: strike – struck – struck.

items.pattern: form / develop a (lasting / close) friendship (with sb)
items.meaning: build a friendship that becomes strong and lasts
items.example: My grandparents **formed a lasting friendship** with the couple across the street, and the two families still spend every New Year together.
more: The two nurses **formed a close friendship** during the long night shifts.
She **developed a real friendship** with her piano teacher over ten years of lessons.
items.watchOut: «Подружитися» — make friends, а «зав'язати дружбу» — form або develop a friendship. Make a friendship зазвичай не кажуть: make поєднується з friends (людьми), а не з friendship.

items.pattern: cement a friendship / relationship · sth cements a friendship
items.meaning: make a friendship stronger and more solid
items.example: Helping each other through a difficult year **cemented** their **friendship**.
more: Working side by side on the school play **cemented** the girls' **friendship**.
Their shared love of fishing **cemented** the **friendship** between my dad and my husband.

items.pattern: spoil a friendship / relationship · spoil – spoilt / spoiled
items.meaning: harm a friendship so that it is not as good as before
items.example: She was afraid that telling him the truth would **spoil** their **friendship**.
more: Sharing a flat **spoilt** our **friendship**: we argued about the washing-up every day.
A silly argument about football **spoilt** their **friendship** for months.
items.watchOut: «Зіпсувати дружбу» — spoil або damage a friendship. Якщо дружбу розірвали зовсім — end або break off a friendship. Минулий час: британською частіше spoilt, американською — spoiled.

items.pattern: a friendship grows (stronger / closer) · grow – grew – grown
items.meaning: a friendship gets stronger and closer over time
items.example: Our **friendship grew** over many cups of tea in her tiny kitchen.
more: Their **friendship grew** stronger with every letter they wrote.
Over the years, our **friendship** has **grown** into something like family.
items.watchOut: Дружба «росте», як рослина: our friendship grew (stronger). Increase тут зазвичай не кажуть: increase — про кількість і числа (prices increase).

items.pattern: close / special friends · a close / special friend
items.meaning: friends you know very well and care about a lot
items.example: Only a few **close friends** knew that we were planning to get married.
more: Olena is a **special friend**: she's been there for me since we were six.
My brother and his wife are **close friends** with the couple next door.
items.watchOut: «Близький друг» — a close friend, а не a near friend: near — про відстань (лише про родину кажуть a near relative, my nearest and dearest). Вимова: close «близький» — /kləʊs/ з глухим s; close «зачиняти» — /kləʊz/.

items.pattern: a mutual friend · mutual friends · also friends in common
items.meaning: friends that you and another person both have
items.example: I met my husband through a **mutual friend** who invited us both to her birthday party.
more: We've got lots of **mutual friends**, so we see each other at most parties.
After the divorce, they tried not to make their **mutual friends** take sides.
items.watchOut: «Спільні друзі» — mutual friends або friends in common: We have a lot of friends in common. Common friends іноді чути, але природніше mutual. Наголос на перший склад: MU-tual.

items.pattern: a casual acquaintance · an acquaintance of mine · just acquaintances
items.meaning: someone you know a little, but not well enough to call a friend
items.example: Most of the guests at the wedding were **casual acquaintances** of the groom, people he'd met through work.
more: My dad stops to chat with every **casual acquaintance** he meets in the street.
An **acquaintance** of mine runs a guesthouse by the sea, so I asked her about prices.
items.watchOut: «Знайомий» — an acquaintance або простіше someone I know. «Мій знайомий» часто кажуть a friend of mine, навіть коли людина не дуже близька. Наголос на другий склад: ac-QUAIN-tance.

items.phrase: have a good relationship with sb
items.pattern: have a good / close / difficult relationship with sb
items.meaning: get on well with someone
items.example: I **have a good relationship with** my mother-in-law: we go shopping together every month.
more: The new manager **has a good relationship with** everyone in the team.
My brother and I **have a** much **better relationship** now that we don't share a room.
items.watchOut: Між двома людьми — a relationship (в однині): I have a good relationship with my sister. Relations (у множині) звучить офіційно й частіше про країни, компанії, групи: diplomatic relations. А a relation — ще й родич.

items.pattern: keep in touch / contact (with sb) · stay in touch · be / get in touch
items.meaning: continue to talk, write to or meet someone, even though you don't see them often
items.example: We went to different universities, but we've **kept in touch** for twenty years.
more: Let's **keep in contact** while you're working abroad.
My grandma **keeps in touch with** her cousins in the village by phone.
items.watchOut: «Підтримувати зв'язок» — keep in touch / contact (with sb), а не support contact чи hold contact. «Будемо на зв'язку!» — Let's keep in touch! або I'll be in touch. Contact тут в однині.

items.pattern: lose touch / contact (with sb) · ↔ keep in touch
items.meaning: stop talking or writing to someone, so you no longer know what is happening in their life
items.example: We **lost touch** after university, but last year we found each other again.
more: I've **lost contact with** most of the people from my first job.
It's easy to **lose touch** with old friends when you have small children.
items.watchOut: Порівняй: keep IN touch, але lose touch — без in і без артикля. Не lose in touch і не lose the contact.

items.pattern: fall in love (with sb / sth) · fall – fell – fallen · be in love (with sb)
items.meaning: start to have strong romantic feelings for someone
items.example: My parents **fell in love** on a school trip to the mountains when they were seventeen.
more: She **fell in love with** the cottage the moment she saw its garden.
Are you still **in love with** him after all these years?
items.watchOut: «Закохатися в когось» — fall in love WITH sb, а не in sb, into sb чи to sb. Закохатися можна і в місто чи річ: I fell in love with Lisbon. Форми: fall – fell – fallen.

items.pattern: be / fall madly in love (with sb) · informal: be crazy about sb
items.meaning: loving someone so strongly that it feels almost crazy
items.example: Grandad still says he **fell madly in love** with Grandma the day she laughed at his terrible joke.
more: They're **madly in love**: they hold hands even when they're doing the shopping.
At fifteen I was **madly in love** with a singer whose poster covered my bedroom wall.
items.watchOut: «Шалено закоханий» — madly in love, а не strongly чи crazily in love. Розмовний варіант — be crazy about sb: He's crazy about her.

items.pattern: be desperately in love (with sb) · also hopelessly in love
items.meaning: loving someone so much that it almost hurts and you badly want to be with them
items.example: In the old film, a poor painter is **desperately in love** with a rich man's daughter.
more: He wrote her a long letter every day: he was **desperately in love**.
When I was a student, I was **desperately in love** with a girl who didn't even know my name.
items.watchOut: Desperately тут не «у розпачі», а «дуже сильно, аж до болю»: desperately in love, desperately want sth (дуже хотіти). «У розпачі» — in despair.

items.pattern: love at first sight · it was love at first sight · fall in love at first sight
items.meaning: falling in love with someone (or something) the moment you first see them
items.example: When my sister saw her future husband at a friend's barbecue, it was **love at first sight**.
more: For my parents it wasn't **love at first sight**: they argued for months before their first date.
The moment I walked into this flat, it was **love at first sight**, and I signed the contract that day.
items.watchOut: «З першого погляду» — at first sight, а не from first sight чи from the first look. Не плутай з at first glance — «на перший погляд», поки не придивився: At first glance, the flat looked fine.

items.pattern: the love of my / your / his / her life
items.meaning: the person you love more than anyone else in your whole life
items.example: Grandma still calls Grandad **the love of her life**, after fifty years of marriage.
more: He was sure the girl from the café was **the love of his life**, but she moved away a month later.
Some people meet **the love of their life** at school, others at sixty.
items.watchOut: «Кохання всього мого життя» — the love of my life, без all. Так кажуть про людину: He's the love of my life.

items.pattern: return sb's love / feelings · sb's love is (not) returned
items.meaning: love someone who loves you
items.example: He adored her for years, but sadly she never **returned his love**.
more: It took him a whole summer to find out that his **love was returned**.
She liked him as a friend but couldn't **return his feelings**.
items.watchOut: «Відповісти взаємністю» — return sb's love або feelings, а не answer sb's love: answer — відповісти на питання, лист, дзвінок. Нерозділене кохання — unrequited love.

items.pattern: make a commitment (to sb / to do sth) · a big / serious / long-term commitment
items.meaning: seriously promise to stay with someone, or to do something, for a long time
items.uk: взяти на себе зобов'язання (всерйоз пов'язати життя з кимось)
items.example: After five years of dating, they felt ready to **make a commitment** and buy a flat.
more: He likes her a lot, but he isn't ready to **make a commitment** yet.
When you **make a commitment** to someone, you stay with them in good times and bad.
items.watchOut: Commitment — серйозне довготривале зобов'язання, а не просто обіцянка. Дієслово — make: make a commitment, а не do a commitment. Пишеться з двома m і одним t (а committee — з двома t).

items.pattern: accept / turn down sb's proposal · propose (to sb)
items.meaning: say yes when someone asks you to marry them
items.example: He asked her to marry him on top of a mountain, and she **accepted his proposal** with tears in her eyes.
more: My aunt turned down three **proposals** before she met my uncle.
His mum was the first person to hear that his girlfriend had **accepted his proposal**.
items.watchOut: «Зробити пропозицію» — propose (to sb) або ask sb to marry you. «Прийняти пропозицію» — accept sb's proposal, а відмовити — turn it down. Proposal буває й діловою пропозицією; щоб було ясно, кажуть a marriage proposal.

items.pattern: love sb unconditionally · love each other unconditionally · unconditional love
items.meaning: love someone completely, whatever they do, without asking for anything in return
items.example: Real friends **love** you **unconditionally**: they don't care if you're successful or not.
more: She **loved** him **unconditionally** and forgave him every mistake.
Every child needs **unconditional love** from at least one adult.
items.watchOut: Unconditionally — «беззастережно, без жодних умов». Але «безумовно» у значенні «звичайно, звісно» — certainly або of course, а не unconditionally.

items.pattern: have an affair (with sb) · be having an affair
items.meaning: have a secret romantic and sexual relationship with someone when you or they are married
items.example: In the TV series, the hotel owner is **having an affair** with his wife's best friend.
more: Everyone in the village knew he'd **had an affair**, except his wife.
She found out about the **affair** when she saw a text on his phone.
items.watchOut: Affair тут не «справа»: have an affair — мати таємний роман, коли хтось у шлюбі. Кажуть have an affair, а не make чи do an affair, і не have a novel (novel — роман-книжка). Звичайні стосунки — a relationship.

items.pattern: the object of sb's love / affection(s) · a bit literary or humorous
items.meaning: the person (or thing) that someone loves
items.example: My son spent the whole party staring at **the object of his affection**, a girl from his chemistry class.
more: **The object of my love** at the age of seven was our neighbour's cat.
She sent flowers to **the object of her love** without signing the card.
items.watchOut: Звучить книжно й часто з гумором. Частіше кажуть the object of sb's affection(s). Іменник object — наголос на перший склад /ˈɒbdʒɪkt/, а дієслово to object (заперечувати) — на другий.

warmup.q: I quickly ___ friends with my neighbours.
warmup.explain: Подружитися з кимось — make friends with sb. Find friends with і get friends with так не кажуть.
Близький друг — a close friend /kləʊs/. Near — про відстань: near the station; a near friend сьогодні не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Ми з сестрою маємо гарні стосунки.
warmup.q: My sister and I have a good ___.
warmup.explain: Між двома людьми — a relationship. A relation — родич, relations — офіційні стосунки між країнами чи компаніями.
Спільні друзі — mutual friends або friends in common.

warmup.uk: Давай не губитися — будемо на зв'язку!
warmup.explain: Підтримувати зв'язок — keep in touch або keep in contact (в однині).
Закохатися в когось — fall in love with sb.

warmup.uk: Це було кохання з першого погляду.
warmup.explain: З першого погляду — at first sight. At first glance — «на перший погляд», поки не придивився.

warmup.uk: Вона так і не відповіла йому взаємністю.
warmup.explain: Відповісти взаємністю — return sb's love. Answer — відповісти на питання чи лист.

A.q: Lena and I met at a yoga class and ___ up a friendship over coffee afterwards.
A.explain: Зав'язати дружбу — strike up a friendship; struck — минулий час.

A.q: We hadn't spoken for years: we'd ___ touch after school.
A.explain: Втратити зв'язок — lose touch, без in. Протилежне — keep in touch.

A.q: I only know him to say hello to. He's just a casual ___.
A.explain: Малознайома людина — a casual acquaintance. Friendship — сама дружба, а не людина; a relation — родич.

B.q: Who was the first person you fell in love ___?
B.explain: Закохатися в когось — fall in love with sb.

B.q: So did she say yes? Did she ___ your proposal?
B.explain: Прийняти пропозицію — accept sb's proposal; відмовити — turn it down.

B.q: Everyone was shocked when they found out he'd been ___ an affair with his neighbour.
B.explain: Мати таємний роман — have an affair, а не make чи do.

example.title: How my grandparents met
example.uk:
У 1975 році моя бабуся поїхала на курси англійської в Брайтон. Першого ж дня вона зав'язала дружбу з дівчиною з Уельсу, і через цю спільну подругу познайомилася з моїм дідусем. Бабуся каже, що це було кохання з першого погляду, і, на її радість, він відповів їй взаємністю.

Коли наприкінці літа вона поїхала додому, вони обмінялися адресами й пообіцяли підтримувати зв'язок. Цілий рік вони щотижня писали одне одному довгі листи, і він став коханням усього її життя. А потім одного зимового вечора він постукав у її двері й попросив її вийти за нього заміж. Звісно, вона прийняла його пропозицію.

Минуло п'ятдесят років, а вони й досі люблять одне одного беззастережно і ніколи не втрачали зв'язку зі своєю подругою з Уельсу.
example.en:
In 1975 my grandmother went on an English course in Brighton. On the first day she [[struck up a friendship|a2]] with a girl from Wales, and through this [[mutual friend|a8]] she met my grandfather. Grandma says it was [[love at first sight|b4]], and to her delight, he [[returned her love|b6]].

When she went home at the end of the summer, they swapped addresses and promised to [[keep in touch|a11]]. For a whole year they wrote long letters every week, and he became [[the love of her life|b5]]. Then one winter evening he knocked at her door and asked her to marry him. Of course, she [[accepted his proposal|b8]].

Fifty years later, they still [[love each other unconditionally|b9]], and they have never [[lost touch|a12]] with their friend from Wales.
